_note: v3.9 world-graph knobs (combat-spec §12-§13, world-graph.md §4). camelCase like balance.json; stays its own file (src/data/world/world_rules.json, GameDev). Tuned with build/world/world_sim.py. Not repeated here (already in balance.json): patrol trigger learning.bossTrigger / bossTriggerSpeech, forced patrols learning.patrolsPerTrip, patrol elite learning.eliteReplaceChance, max enemies combat.maxEnemies, Return Feather item = shop.json 'feather' (its v3.9 price and rules are in returnFeather below).

afterBossClear.scope: the way you came: the shortest route over already-walked (or safe) edges from the cleared boss / mini-boss node back to the nearest inn or town; never the unexplored way forward

townDensity.rule: v3.9.1: towns + villages per realm = max(1, ceil(nodes / (20 + 5 x (realm - 1)))), counting the main town, so a settlement never serves more than 20, 25 ... 60 nodes

realmBossFeather.note: v3.9.1: the realm-boss chest of these realms also holds a free Return Feather (on: clear event on the boss node). No shop nudge or tip.

returnFeather.destinationRule: v3.9.2: exactly two kinds of destination. lastInn = the one node where the player last rested (an inn, a campfire inn, or the inn of a town or village); it is replaced each time the player rests. visitedTown = every node of kind town or village the player has ever entered, in any realm. Inns other than the last one used are never destinations, even if visited.
returnFeather.usable: anywhere on the map outside battle and outside a boss room
returnFeather.note: v3.9: no free warp. A Feather is the only fast way back to a town (and from a town back to the last inn). Sold in town and village item shops, not at inns.

fog.reveal: visited nodes + every node one open edge away from a visited node (shown as '?', kind hidden)
fog.state: player progress (progress.schema.json: visited / walked bitsets by idx); never stored in the graph file

seed.hashRule: v3.9.2: seed = FNV-1a 32-bit of the key string (offset basis 0x811c9dc5, prime 0x01000193, XOR each UTF-16 code unit then multiply mod 2^32; keys are ASCII so code units = bytes); roll = first mulberry32 output (uint32 / 2^32, in [0,1)). A battle starts when roll < chance.
seed.note: every roll is a pure function of the save seed and how many times that edge was crossed, so reloading never re-rolls
